description: Question bank based on Government Rural Development Programmes (FDA & SDA Exam Notes). Verify and expand questions before formal examination use.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What are Government rural development programmes?

options.A: Policies, schemes and missions implemented by Union and State Governments to reduce rural poverty, improve livelihoods, create employment, provide basic services and develop village infrastructure
options.B: Only policies implemented by the Union Government for urban development
options.C: Programmes implemented exclusively by private companies for rural profit
options.D: Schemes implemented only by Gram Panchayats without government funding

questions.explanation: They are policies, schemes and missions implemented by the Union and State Governments to reduce rural poverty, improve livelihoods, create employment, provide basic services and develop village infrastructure.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: Which Union Ministry implements many of India's major rural development schemes?

options.A: Ministry of Jal Shakti
options.B: Ministry of Rural Development
options.C: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

questions.explanation: The Ministry of Rural Development implements major programmes relating to rural employment, housing, roads, livelihoods and social assistance.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: Which Ministry is responsible for Jal Jeevan Mission and Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen?

options.A: Ministry of Rural Development
options.B: Ministry of Jal Shakti, through the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation
options.C: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
options.D: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

questions.explanation: The Ministry of Jal Shakti, through the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, is responsible for these rural drinking-water and sanitation missions.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: Which Ministry implements major national skill development programmes?

options.A: Ministry of Rural Development
options.B: Ministry of Jal Shakti
options.C: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

questions.explanation: The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship is the nodal ministry for major national skill development initiatives, while several other ministries also run sector-specific skill programmes.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme?

options.A: A programme financed and implemented solely by the Union Government
options.B: A programme in which the Union Government and State Governments share funding and implementation responsibilities according to a prescribed ratio
options.C: A programme implemented only by Panchayati Raj Institutions
options.D: A programme funded entirely by international organizations

questions.explanation: A Centrally Sponsored Scheme is a programme in which the Union Government and State Governments share funding and implementation responsibilities according to a prescribed ratio.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is a Central Sector Scheme?

options.A: A scheme generally financed and implemented by the Union Government, rather than through the usual Centre-State cost-sharing arrangement
options.B: A scheme funded entirely by State Governments
options.C: A scheme implemented by private sector companies
options.D: A scheme funded by foreign governments

questions.explanation: A Central Sector Scheme is generally financed and implemented by the Union Government, rather than through the usual Centre-State cost-sharing arrangement.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is scheme convergence?

options.A: Coordinating two or more government schemes so that a household or village receives complementary services and infrastructure instead of isolated benefits
options.B: Merging all government schemes into a single scheme
options.D: Transferring scheme funds to private accounts

questions.explanation: Convergence means coordinating two or more government schemes so that a household or village receives complementary services and infrastructure instead of isolated benefits.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: Why are Gram Panchayats important in rural development programmes?

options.A: They only collect taxes from villagers
options.B: They help identify local needs, prepare village plans, facilitate beneficiary participation, implement or supervise works and monitor public assets, subject to the rules of each scheme
options.C: They have no role in rural development programmes
options.D: They only distribute subsidies to beneficiaries

questions.explanation: Gram Panchayats help identify local needs, prepare village plans, facilitate beneficiary participation, implement or supervise works and monitor public assets, subject to the rules of each scheme.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)?

options.A: Electronic transfer of eligible benefits directly to a beneficiary's bank account, intended to improve transparency and reduce intermediaries
options.B: Transfer of benefits in cash by government officials
options.C: Transfer of benefits through post offices only
options.D: Transfer of benefits through private banks only

questions.explanation: DBT is the electronic transfer of eligible benefits directly to a beneficiary's bank account, intended to improve transparency and reduce intermediaries.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is social audit?

options.A: An audit conducted by private chartered accountants
options.B: A community-based verification of programme records, expenditure, works and entitlements, intended to strengthen transparency and accountability
options.C: An audit conducted only by government officials
options.D: An audit of social media accounts

questions.explanation: A social audit is a community-based verification of programme records, expenditure, works and entitlements, intended to strengthen transparency and accountability.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What was the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)?

options.A: A rights-based law enacted in 2005 to enhance livelihood security in rural India by guaranteeing wage employment to rural households whose adult members volunteered for unskilled manual work
options.B: A law enacted in 2010 to provide urban employment
options.C: A scheme to provide free food grains to rural households
options.D: A programme to provide housing to rural poor

questions.explanation: It was a rights-based law enacted in 2005 to enhance livelihood security in rural India by guaranteeing wage employment to rural households whose adult members volunteered for unskilled manual work.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: When was the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act enacted?
questions.explanation: It was enacted in 2005.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: When was the Act renamed MGNREGA?
questions.explanation: It was renamed the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act in 2009.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What was the employment guarantee under MGNREGA?

options.A: At least 100 days of unskilled manual wage employment per financial year to each eligible rural household
options.B: At least 100 days of employment to each adult member separately
options.C: At least 150 days of employment per household
options.D: At least 125 days of employment per household

questions.explanation: It guaranteed at least 100 days of unskilled manual wage employment per financial year to each eligible rural household, subject to the Act.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: Was the MGNREGA guarantee given to each adult separately?

options.A: Yes, 100 days for every adult member
options.B: No, the 100-day guarantee was for the rural household, not 100 days for every adult member
options.C: Yes, but only for male adults
options.D: Yes, but only for female adults

questions.explanation: No. The 100-day guarantee was for the rural household, not 100 days for every adult member.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What was the main objective of MGNREGA?

options.A: To enhance rural livelihood security through guaranteed wage employment and the creation of durable community and household assets
options.B: To provide free education to rural children
options.C: To provide free healthcare to rural households
options.D: To provide urban employment to rural migrants

questions.explanation: Its objective was to enhance rural livelihood security through guaranteed wage employment and the creation of durable community and household assets.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: Which institution issued the job card under MGNREGA?

options.A: Block Development Office
options.B: Gram Panchayat

questions.explanation: The Gram Panchayat registered eligible households and issued job cards under the Act and its rules.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is a job card?

options.A: A card issued by banks for opening accounts
options.B: An official record of a registered household and its adult members who are willing to undertake unskilled manual work under the employment guarantee programme

questions.explanation: A job card is an official record of a registered household and its adult members who are willing to undertake unskilled manual work under the employment guarantee programme.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: Within what period was work to be provided after a valid demand under MGNREGA?

options.A: 7 days
options.B: 10 days

questions.explanation: Employment was to be provided within 15 days of the application or from the date work was sought, as prescribed by the Act.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What was the unemployment allowance under MGNREGA?

options.A: If work was not provided within the prescribed period after a valid demand, the applicant household became entitled to unemployment allowance under the conditions and rates prescribed by the Act
options.B: A fixed allowance of Rs. 100 per day to all rural households
options.C: An allowance paid only to landless households
options.D: An allowance paid only to women workers

questions.explanation: If work was not provided within the prescribed period after a valid demand, the applicant household became entitled to unemployment allowance under the conditions and rates prescribed by the Act.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is a muster roll?

options.A: A list of beneficiaries for housing scheme
options.B: The official attendance and work record of labourers engaged on a public work
options.C: A list of village council members

questions.explanation: A muster roll is the official attendance and work record of labourers engaged on a public work.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the purpose of social audit under MGNREGA?

options.A: To enable villagers to verify muster rolls, wage payments, expenditure, work quality and compliance with entitlements in a public and participatory process
options.B: To audit the personal accounts of government officials
options.C: To conduct financial audit by chartered accountants
options.D: To audit the performance of private contractors

questions.explanation: It enables villagers to verify muster rolls, wage payments, expenditure, work quality and compliance with entitlements in a public and participatory process.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What kinds of assets were created under MGNREGA?

options.A: Only roads and bridges
options.B: Permissible works included water conservation, drought proofing, irrigation facilities, land development, flood control, rural connectivity and other notified categories of productive rural assets

questions.explanation: Permissible works included water conservation, drought proofing, irrigation facilities, land development, flood control, rural connectivity and other notified categories of productive rural assets.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the difference between MGNREGA and MGNREGS?

options.A: MGNREGA refers to the Act, while MGNREGS refers to the scheme implemented under that legislation
options.B: MGNREGA is for rural areas, MGNREGS is for urban areas
options.C: MGNREGA is for men, MGNREGS is for women

questions.explanation: MGNREGA refers to the Act, while MGNREGS refers to the scheme implemented under that legislation.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: When did MGNREGA cease to operate as the national statutory framework?

options.A: 31 March 2026
options.B: 1 July 2026

questions.explanation: It was repealed with effect from 1 July 2026, when the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 came into force.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the full form of VB-G RAM G?

options.A: Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)
options.B: Village Bharat-Guarantee for Rural Agriculture Mission (Gramin)
options.C: Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rural Area Management (Gramin)
options.D: Village Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)

questions.explanation: Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin).

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: Which law established the VB-G RAM G framework?

options.A: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005
options.B: The Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025
options.C: The National Rural Livelihoods Mission Act, 2011

questions.explanation: The Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: When did the VB-G RAM G Act come into force nationwide?

options.A: 1 January 2026
options.B: 1 April 2026

questions.explanation: It came into force on 1 July 2026.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: How many days of wage employment are guaranteed under VB-G RAM G?

options.A: 100 days
options.B: 125 days

questions.explanation: The Act provides a statutory guarantee of 125 days of wage employment in each financial year to every eligible rural household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: Is the 125-day guarantee under VB-G RAM G an individual or household entitlement?

options.A: Individual entitlement for every adult member
options.B: Household-level entitlement for each financial year, not 125 days for every adult separately

questions.explanation: It is a household-level entitlement for each financial year, not 125 days for every adult separately.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What are the four broad thematic categories of works under VB-G RAM G?

options.A: Water-related works for water security, core rural infrastructure, livelihood-related infrastructure, and special works for mitigating extreme weather events and disasters
options.B: Roads, bridges, schools and hospitals
options.C: Housing, sanitation, drinking water and skill development

questions.explanation: They are water-related works for water security, core rural infrastructure, livelihood-related infrastructure, and special works for mitigating extreme weather events and disasters.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What are Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans?

options.A: Plans prepared by the Union Government for each Gram Panchayat
options.B: Participatory village development plans prepared through Gram Panchayats and Gram Sabhas to identify and prioritise local works under the new framework
options.D: Plans prepared by state governments without local participation

questions.explanation: They are participatory village development plans prepared through Gram Panchayats and Gram Sabhas to identify and prioritise local works under the new framework.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the Viksit Bharat National Rural Infrastructure Stack?

options.A: A digital platform for rural e-commerce
options.B: The integrated aggregation of proposed rural public works emerging from village plans and consolidated at higher administrative levels, aligned with the framework's thematic areas
options.C: A stack of rural infrastructure projects funded by private companies
options.D: A database of rural infrastructure contractors

questions.explanation: It is the integrated aggregation of proposed rural public works emerging from village plans and consolidated at higher administrative levels, aligned with the framework's thematic areas.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the purpose of the 60-day pause provision under VB-G RAM G?

options.A: To pause all rural development works during monsoon
options.B: To provide for an aggregate 60-day pause in works during peak agricultural sowing and harvesting periods to help ensure labour availability for agriculture
options.C: To pause wages during election periods
options.D: To pause new project approvals for 60 days

questions.explanation: The Act provides for an aggregate 60-day pause in works during peak agricultural sowing and harvesting periods to help ensure labour availability for agriculture.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the general Centre-State funding ratio under VB-G RAM G for Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The general ratio for Karnataka and most other States is 60:40, with the Centre contributing 60 per cent and the State 40 per cent.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the funding ratio for specified North-Eastern and Himalayan States under VB-G RAM G?
questions.explanation: The prescribed ratio is 90:10 for the specified North-Eastern States, Himalayan States and the specified Union Territories.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: How are wages paid under VB-G RAM G?

options.A: In cash by government officials
options.B: Wages are transferred directly to workers' bank or post-office accounts through the prescribed digital payment mechanism, with statutory safeguards relating to timely payment and delay compensation
options.C: Through cheques issued by Gram Panchayats

questions.explanation: Wages are transferred directly to workers' bank or post-office accounts through the prescribed digital payment mechanism, with statutory safeguards relating to timely payment and delay compensation.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the key difference between MGNREGA and VB-G RAM G?

options.A: MGNREGA provided 100 days of household wage employment and operated until 30 June 2026; VB-G RAM G provides 125 days and came into force on 1 July 2026
options.B: MGNREGA provided 125 days and VB-G RAM G provides 100 days
options.D: MGNREGA is for urban areas and VB-G RAM G is for rural areas

questions.explanation: MGNREGA provided 100 days of household wage employment and operated until 30 June 2026; VB-G RAM G provides 125 days and came into force on 1 July 2026.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding MGNREGA after 1 July 2026?

options.A: MGNREGA is the current operating Act after 1 July 2026
options.B: MGNREGA remains important for questions on the history of rural employment guarantees, its original 100-day entitlement, job cards, social audits and its transition to VB-G RAM G
options.D: MGNREGA is still operational in some states only

questions.explanation: Exam caution: Do not write that MGNREGA is the current operating Act after 1 July 2026. It remains important for questions on the history of rural employment guarantees, its original 100-day entitlement, job cards, social audits and its transition to VB-G RAM G.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What was Indira Awaas Yojana (IAY)?

options.A: A rural housing assistance programme introduced in 1985-86 to support construction or upgradation of houses for eligible rural poor households
options.B: A rural employment programme

questions.explanation: IAY was a rural housing assistance programme introduced in 1985-86 to support construction or upgradation of houses for eligible rural poor households.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: Which programme replaced IAY?

options.A: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G)
options.B: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)

questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G) restructured and replaced IAY with effect from 1 April 2016.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: When was PMAY-G launched?

options.A: 20 November 2016, with effect from 1 April 2016
options.B: 1 April 2016, with effect from 20 November 2016

questions.explanation: PMAY-G was launched on 20 November 2016, with effect from 1 April 2016.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: Which ministry implements PMAY-G?

options.A: Ministry of Jal Shakti
options.B: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
options.C: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

questions.explanation: The Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the main objective of PMAY-G?

options.A: To provide a pucca house with basic amenities to eligible houseless rural households and households living in kutcha or dilapidated houses
options.B: To provide urban housing to rural migrants
options.C: To provide rental housing in rural areas
options.D: To provide housing loans at subsidized rates

questions.explanation: To provide a pucca house with basic amenities to eligible houseless rural households and households living in kutcha or dilapidated houses.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the minimum house size under PMAY-G?

options.A: 20 square metres
options.B: 25 square metres, including a dedicated area for hygienic cooking

questions.explanation: The minimum house size is 25 square metres, including a dedicated area for hygienic cooking.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the standard unit assistance under PMAY-G in plain areas?

options.A: ₹1.00 lakh per eligible house
options.B: ₹1.20 lakh per eligible house, subject to scheme guidelines

questions.explanation: ₹1.20 lakh per eligible house, subject to scheme guidelines.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the standard unit assistance under PMAY-G in specified hilly and difficult areas?

options.A: ₹1.20 lakh per eligible house
options.B: ₹1.30 lakh per eligible house, subject to scheme guidelines

questions.explanation: ₹1.30 lakh per eligible house, subject to scheme guidelines.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: How are PMAY-G beneficiaries identified?

options.A: Through random selection by district officials
options.B: Using housing deprivation information, applicable eligibility and exclusion criteria, prioritisation rules and Gram Sabha verification
options.D: Through recommendation by Members of Parliament

questions.explanation: Beneficiaries are identified using housing deprivation information, applicable eligibility and exclusion criteria, prioritisation rules and Gram Sabha verification.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the role of the Gram Sabha in PMAY-G?

options.A: It constructs houses
options.B: It verifies the beneficiary list and supports transparency and local accountability in selection

questions.explanation: The Gram Sabha verifies the beneficiary list and supports transparency and local accountability in selection.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is AwaasSoft?

options.A: A mobile application for house construction
options.B: The web-based management information system used for PMAY-G administration and monitoring

questions.explanation: AwaasSoft is the web-based management information system used for PMAY-G administration and monitoring.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is AwaasApp?

options.A: A mobile application used for geo-tagged and time-stamped monitoring of house construction progress
options.B: A web portal for PMAY-G

questions.explanation: AwaasApp is a mobile application used for geo-tagged and time-stamped monitoring of house construction progress.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the objective of PM-JANMAN housing support?

options.A: To provide housing to urban poor
options.B: PM-JANMAN includes targeted housing and other basic-service interventions for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)
options.C: To provide housing to all rural households
options.D: To provide housing to government employees

questions.explanation: PM-JANMAN includes targeted housing and other basic-service interventions for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs).

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the difference between PMAY-G and PMAY-Urban?

options.A: PMAY-G is for eligible rural households, whereas PMAY-Urban addresses eligible urban households
options.B: PMAY-G is for urban households, whereas PMAY-Urban addresses rural households

questions.explanation: PMAY-G is for eligible rural households, whereas PMAY-Urban addresses eligible urban households.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is DAY-NRLM?

options.A: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission, a centrally sponsored programme of the Ministry of Rural Development to reduce rural poverty by building strong community institutions of poor women and improving access to finance, skills, livelihoods and markets
options.B: A rural housing programme

questions.explanation: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission is a centrally sponsored programme of the Ministry of Rural Development to reduce rural poverty by building strong community institutions of poor women and improving access to finance, skills, livelihoods and markets.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: When was the National Rural Livelihoods Mission launched?

options.A: June 2011
options.B: April 2011

questions.explanation: NRLM was launched in June 2011.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What was the earlier name of NRLM?

options.A: Aajeevika
options.B: Swarna Jayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana

questions.explanation: It was earlier known as Aajeevika; it is now implemented as DAY-NRLM.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the core strategy of DAY-NRLM?

options.A: Providing direct cash transfers to rural poor
options.B: Social mobilisation of rural poor women into self-help groups and their federations, followed by institution building, financial inclusion and sustainable livelihood support
options.C: Providing free food grains to rural poor
options.D: Providing employment guarantee to rural households

questions.explanation: Its core strategy is social mobilisation of rural poor women into self-help groups and their federations, followed by institution building, financial inclusion and sustainable livelihood support.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What are the four broad components of DAY-NRLM?

options.A: Social mobilisation and institution building, financial inclusion, sustainable livelihoods, and social inclusion/social development/convergence
options.B: Housing, sanitation, drinking water and skill development

questions.explanation: The four components are social mobilisation and institution building, financial inclusion, sustainable livelihoods, and social inclusion/social development/convergence.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is a Self-Help Group under DAY-NRLM?

options.A: A member-based community institution, generally comprising 10-20 women, who save regularly, lend internally and undertake collective social and economic activities
options.B: A group of 50-100 men who work on infrastructure projects
options.C: A government committee for rural development
options.D: A private company operating in rural areas

questions.explanation: It is a member-based community institution, generally comprising 10-20 women, who save regularly, lend internally and undertake collective social and economic activities.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is a Village Organisation under DAY-NRLM?

options.A: A federation of SHGs at village level that supports group strengthening, financial intermediation and collective livelihood action
options.B: A government office at village level
options.D: A private bank branch in a village

questions.explanation: A Village Organisation is a federation of SHGs at village level that supports group strengthening, financial intermediation and collective livelihood action.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is a Cluster Level Federation?

options.A: A higher-level community institution that federates Village Organisations or SHGs across a cluster and provides coordination and support
options.B: A federation of banks
options.C: A government committee at block level

questions.explanation: A Cluster Level Federation is a higher-level community institution that federates Village Organisations or SHGs across a cluster and provides coordination and support.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the Revolving Fund under DAY-NRLM?

options.A: Financial assistance provided to eligible SHGs to strengthen their corpus and support internal lending and financial discipline
options.B: A fund that rotates among government departments
options.D: A fund for purchasing agricultural equipment

questions.explanation: It is financial assistance provided to eligible SHGs to strengthen their corpus and support internal lending and financial discipline.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the Community Investment Fund under DAY-NRLM?

options.A: A community-level fund routed through eligible community institutions to support livelihood investment plans and income-generating activities
options.B: A fund for community infrastructure

questions.explanation: It is a community-level fund routed through eligible community institutions to support livelihood investment plans and income-generating activities.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is SHG-Bank Linkage?

options.A: A programme that links self-help groups with formal banks for savings and credit services; NABARD launched it as a pilot in 1992
options.B: A programme that links SHGs with private moneylenders
options.C: A programme that links SHGs with foreign banks
options.D: A programme that links SHGs with insurance companies

questions.explanation: SHG-Bank Linkage is a programme that links self-help groups with formal banks for savings and credit services; NABARD launched it as a pilot in 1992.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the Lakhpati Didi initiative?

options.A: It seeks to enable women SHG members to earn a sustainable annual household income of at least ₹1 lakh through diversified livelihood activities and enterprise development
options.B: It provides ₹1 lakh to every rural woman
options.C: It provides ₹1 lakh to every SHG
options.D: It provides ₹1 lakh to every Gram Panchayat

questions.explanation: It seeks to enable women SHG members to earn a sustainable annual household income of at least ₹1 lakh through diversified livelihood activities and enterprise development.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP)?

options.A: SVEP supports rural poor households, particularly SHG members and their families, to establish and grow non-farm micro-enterprises through training, mentoring, finance and business support
options.B: SVEP supports urban start-ups
options.C: SVEP supports large industries in rural areas
options.D: SVEP supports government offices in rural areas

questions.explanation: SVEP supports rural poor households, particularly SHG members and their families, to establish and grow non-farm micro-enterprises through training, mentoring, finance and business support.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana (MKSP)?

options.A: MKSP is a DAY-NRLM sub-component that promotes the empowerment and improved livelihoods of women farmers through sustainable agriculture and allied activities
options.B: A programme for women's education

questions.explanation: MKSP is a DAY-NRLM sub-component that promotes the empowerment and improved livelihoods of women farmers through sustainable agriculture and allied activities.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is a Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO)?

options.A: A collective of farmers formed to improve economies of scale, access to inputs and technology, aggregation, processing, credit and marketing
options.B: A government department for farmers
options.C: A private company owned by farmers

questions.explanation: An FPO is a collective of farmers formed to improve economies of scale, access to inputs and technology, aggregation, processing, credit and marketing.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the National Rural Economic Transformation Project (NRETP)?

options.A: NRETP was a World Bank-supported initiative designed to strengthen selected DAY-NRLM interventions, including enterprise promotion, financial inclusion and market access; its project period and current status should be distinguished from the continuing DAY-NRLM mission
options.B: A government programme for rural infrastructure

questions.explanation: NRETP was a World Bank-supported initiative designed to strengthen selected DAY-NRLM interventions, including enterprise promotion, financial inclusion and market access; its project period and current status should be distinguished from the continuing DAY-NRLM mission.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is the role of cooperatives in rural livelihoods?

options.A: Cooperatives allow members to pool resources, obtain inputs and credit, process products and market collectively, thereby improving bargaining power and member benefits
options.B: Cooperatives only provide loans

questions.explanation: Cooperatives allow members to pool resources, obtain inputs and credit, process products and market collectively, thereby improving bargaining power and member benefits.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: What is Swachh Bharat Mission-Grameen (SBM-G)?

options.A: The rural component of Swachh Bharat Mission, launched to improve sanitation, eliminate open defecation and promote cleanliness and waste management in villages
options.B: The urban component of Swachh Bharat Mission

questions.explanation: SBM-G is the rural component of Swachh Bharat Mission, launched to improve sanitation, eliminate open defecation and promote cleanliness and waste management in villages.

questions.subject: Rural Development
questions.question: When was Swachh Bharat Mission launched?
